role: Regional planning commission that adopted highway interim plan
stance_basis: letter stating project conditionally consistent with regional planning, with construction contingent on Park Forest Consolidation Study findings, later upgraded to fully consistent after condition was resolved
summary: The Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission (Metropolitan Clearinghouse) initially found the proposed Lincoln Highway project to be only conditionally consistent with comprehensive regional planning, requiring affirmative findings from the Park Forest Consolidation Study before construction could proceed. After that study was cancelled by the Village of Park Forest, the condition was lifted, and at a May 8, 1974 meeting the Commission found the project fully consistent with regional planning policies. The Interstate Planning Committee also concurred with this final positive finding.
complaint_summary: At a May 8, 1974 meeting, the Commission's Planning Committee found the project to be fully consistent with regional planning policies as set forth in the Comprehensive General Plan and currently adopted Commission plans and programs, removing the earlier conditional finding.
summary_quote: The Commission, through its Planning Committee, found the proposed project to be conditionally consistent with comprehensive regional planning. While the Committee recommended that the Illinois Department of Transportation will be allowed to proceed with the acquisition of land and design approval for the project, actual construction is not to take place until a receipt of affirmative findings has been obtained from the Park Forest Consolidation Study.

mentions.quote: Lincoln Highway is shown as an arterial in the Chicago Area Transportation Study Highway Interim Plan which was adopted By the Northeastern Illinois Planning Commission on October 21, 1971, as one of its functional plans
